text: hey everybody most Scholars who study early Israelite religion are in pretty General agreement that in the earliest periods of Israel's history the god of
Israel first L and then the conflated L and Adonai had a wife named Ashura and
almost 3 000 years ago it seems like someone in the Sinai Peninsula drew a picture of both the god of Israel and
their consort or wife ashra this is a photograph of the relevant part of this large pot and it's a little difficult to
see what's going on here so here is a drawing I did of that artifact and you can see there's an inscription that was
written over top of the male deity figure it could have been written by the person who did the drawings more likely
it was written by someone else but they talk about blessings and then on the very bottom line of the inscription the line that is centered over the male
deity and overlaps their headdress says by Adonai of shomran and by ashara so
this inscription most likely understands the two deities to represent Adonai the god of Israel and their consort Ashura
the goddess of Israel now a common response to this is that this is no big deal because the Bible tells us that
there were apostate Israelites who were worshiping ashra as the Queen of Heaven but the problem with this is that the
only negative references that we have to Ashura in the biblical texts are dated by Scholars to the reign of Josiah and
after they are part of the deuteronomistic literature and the literature that would be influenced by it so they date to the end of the 7th
Century BCE and later and are probably the product of Josiah's campaign of cult centralization we have absolutely no
data from prior to the reign of Josiah that indicates anyone really had a problem with the worship of ashra and
all of the material remains that we have that attest to that worship come from before that time period if you're
interested in reading more about Ashura as an early Israelite goddess Bill deaver's 2005 book did God have a wife
is probably the most General and accessible discussion but Saul Olean is a wonderful scholar who wrote a book on this many years ago
entitled ashra and the cult of Adonai in Israel tilde Binger also has a wonderful volume discussing this
I would highly recommend Judith Hadley's volume The Cult of ashra in ancient Israel and Judah evidence for a Hebrew goddess
Steve Wiggins also has a very careful volume entitled a reassessment of a ashra with further considerations of the
Goddess that seeks to try to temper what Steve sees as some of the excesses of earlier theories
and for great discussion of why it is likely that the two figures that appear on that drawing are indeed Adonai and
his ashra Ryan Thomas has a wonderful article from the Journal of ancient near Eastern religions entitled the identity of the standing figures on pithos a from
quintillidajrude a reassessment and I also discussed some of the Divine Images associated with ashra in my own book adonai's Divine Images a cognitive
approach which is an Open Access volume that you can find for free online and there is a link directly to a PDF of the
book in my link tree I also taught an online class last year on the Israelite goddess ashra and you can purchase access to that recording and to the
recordings of other online classes that I have taught at mcclellan.org
